name: Prostate cancer
theme: the risk ladder · the intensification era

meta.title: Prostate cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.population: Adults with prostate adenocarcinoma across the whole arc: the risk ladder in localized disease (where the honest first question is whether treatment is needed at all - ProtecT's 15-year flat line), biochemical recurrence (where the timing rule is early-salvage, not adjuvant), metastatic hormone-sensitive disease (the intensification era, where the named substandard - ADT alone - is still what too many patients actually get), and castration resistance (the MFS trio, the PARP label-scope lessons, the radioligand era with its approval-versus-OS honesty). Small-cell/neuroendocrine transformation is noted as a lineage-plasticity escape under ARPI pressure - platinum-era biology, rerouted with a note. Terminology turn carried: 2026 NCCN and FDA language renames mHSPC/mCSPC to 'metastatic androgen pathway modulation-naive/-sensitive' (mAPMN/S) and uses 'ARPI' throughout - this trainer teaches mHSPC as the primary term with the new name noted.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease with the registry's widest gap between evidence and behavior, at both ends. Localized: ProtecT's 15-year answer renders as a flat line - prostate-cancer mortality ~3% whether monitored, operated, or irradiated (3.1% / 2.2% / 2.9%, p=0.53) - so the low-risk menu ranks nothing and teaches the real currencies: metastases (9.4% vs ~5%), treatment burden, and the quarter of monitored men who never needed treatment at all. High-risk localized carries STAMPEDE M0 abiraterone (6-yr MFS 82% vs 69%). Metastatic hormone-sensitive: the intensification…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: NCCN risk groups (very-low ELIMINATED in the 2026 cycle - folded into low; low / favorable-int / unfavorable-int / high / very-high; secondhand - 403) atop Gleason Grade Groups 1-5; PSMA PET in high-risk staging (proPSMA: accuracy 92% vs 65% for conventional imaging); germline testing for all metastatic and high/very-high localized disease; somatic HRR testing in mCRPC
meta.response: PSA kinetics as the standing response read (with castration status defining the state transitions); PCWG3/RECIST for metastatic trials; MFS as the nmCRPC currency

CRPC routing.label: Castration-resistant context
CRPC routing.help: CRPC is a state, not a symptom: rising PSA WITH castrate testosterone. The nmCRPC label is itself shrinking as PSMA PET reclassifies 'clean scans' - said honestly.
CRPC routing.helpPatient: If the cancer starts moving despite hormone treatment, the next menu depends on whether scans can see it yet.

CRPC routing.label: PSMA PET (for the radioligand)
CRPC routing.help: The theranostic gate: the same scan that stages high-risk disease selects for lutetium-177-PSMA. A PSMA-low tumor is a real minority for whom the newest door honestly does not open.
CRPC routing.helpPatient: A special scan checks whether the cancer displays the target the newest radioactive medicine homes in on.

Newly diagnosed.name: Active surveillance (the flat line's first-class option)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN preferred for low-risk (secondhand); ProtecT randomized basis
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from treatment - the entire point; the costs are the calendar and the uncertainty, named as real
Newly diagnosed.patient: For low-risk disease: careful watching, with treatment held ready. Fifteen years of trial data show survival is the same as immediate surgery or radiation - and a quarter of watched men never needed treatment at all.

Newly diagnosed.name: Radical prostatectomy (same line, different ledger)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x3 (ProtecT, SPCG-4, PIVOT - read by detection era)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the operation's ledger: urinary incontinence and erectile dysfunction lead - permanent for some, and the flat line makes them the actual price
Newly diagnosed.patient: Removing the prostate: survival matches watching and radiation in low-risk disease - what it buys is fewer later spreads, at the cost of the operation's real side effects.

Newly diagnosed.name: Radiation (+ short ADT by flavor) - the third seat at the same table
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: bowel and urinary irritation (mostly transient), the short-ADT ledger where added - a different shape of cost than surgery's, same survival line
Newly diagnosed.patient: Radiation: the third option on the same survival line - different side-effect shape (bowel and urinary rather than surgical), sometimes with a few months of hormone treatment added.

Newly diagnosed.name: RT + long ADT + abiraterone (high/very-high - STAMPEDE M0)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: randomized platform meta-analysis (STAMPEDE M0) - MFS verified; the OS percentage itself flagged
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the full ADT ledger for years plus abiraterone's (pressure, potassium, liver) - the heaviest curative-intent load on this ladder, for the rung that earns it
Newly diagnosed.patient: For high-risk disease still confined to the prostate: radiation plus a long hormone course plus an intensifying tablet - the combination that cut the risk of spread by nearly half.

Newly diagnosed.name: ADT + ARPI (the doublet minimum - mHSPC/mAPMN-S)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x4 (LATITUDE/ENZAMET/ARCHES/TITAN) - OS met repeatedly
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the ADT ledger plus the chosen ARPI's signature (fatigue, hypertension, falls by agent) - years-long, managed as a program
Newly diagnosed.patient: For newly spread, hormone-responsive disease: the hormone injection PLUS a second hormone-pathway tablet - the proven minimum, adding well over a year of median survival versus the injection alone.
drugs: GnRH analog + abiraterone / enzalutamide / apalutamide (darolutamide per ARANOTE, FDA 2025-06)

Newly diagnosed.name: ADT + docetaxel + ARPI (the fit high-volume escalation - ARASENS/PEACE-1)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (ARASENS HR 0.68; PEACE-1) - HRs verified; the median flagged
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: adds chemotherapy's season (counts, neuropathy, fatigue) to the doublet's ledger - the trade fitness buys
Newly diagnosed.patient: For fit patients with a lot of spread disease: adding a chemotherapy season to the hormone combination - the strongest opener, cutting the risk of death by about a third versus the older standard.
drugs: GnRH analog + docetaxel x6 + darolutamide (or abiraterone)

Newly diagnosed.name: ADT alone (the named substandard - displayed on purpose)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: SUBSTANDARD for most patients (guideline-discordant as monotherapy; narrow legitimate uses)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 control arms x many - consistently beaten; the underintensification review verified (BJU Int 2025)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the full ADT ledger WITHOUT the survival benefit of intensification - the worst trade on this menu for most
Newly diagnosed.patient: The hormone injection by itself: the old standard, kept on this menu so the comparison is visible - every modern combination beats it, and if this is what has been offered, asking why is a fair question.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; bone pain and urinary symptom care are the craft
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice - in early disease it overlaps with watching; in spread disease it comes with a team focused on comfort.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: ARPI for nmCRPC (the MFS trio - PROSPER/SPARTAN/ARAMIS)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN category 1 for high-risk nmCRPC (PSADT <=10 months; secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized x3 - MFS decisive, OS confirmed
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: each ARPI's signature (fatigue, falls, rash by agent) on top of the standing ADT ledger
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: When the PSA rises despite hormone treatment but scans stay clean: adding a modern hormone-pathway tablet pushed visible spread back by roughly two years and improved survival.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: PARP inhibitor (BRCA/HRR mCRPC - the label-scope lesson)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: label scopes exactly: olaparib+abi BRCA-only (2023-05); talazoparib+enza HRR-only (2023-06); olaparib mono HRR post-ARPI (all secondhand, p…
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized (PROfound OS met; TALAPRO-2 final OS met in HRR-deficient and all-comers; PROpel all-comers missed)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: anemia leads the class ledger - transfusion-aware monitoring
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If the tumor carries a DNA-repair gene change: targeted tablets extend life - with which exact gene mattering, because the approvals are written gene-by-gene, and the card keeps that straight.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: 177Lu-PSMA-617 (VISION - with the approval-vs-OS honesty attached)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: FDA scope today: PSMA+ mCRPC post-ARPI (taxane before or delayed) + 2026 mHSPC expansion (dates secondhand)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized (VISION OS met; PSMAfore rPFS met / ITT OS NS - both said)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: dry mouth (salivary uptake), cytopenias, fatigue - generally gentler than taxanes; radiation-safety logistics are real
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A radioactive medicine that homes to the cancer's surface marker: proven to extend life after other treatments, now available earlier - where, honestly, it has proven it delays progression but not yet that it lengthens life.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Cabazitaxel (CARD - the sequencing receipt)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: cytopenias (G-CSF standard), diarrhea, neuropathy lighter than docetaxel's
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The second chemotherapy: after the first chemo and a hormone-pathway tablet stop working, this beat trying another tablet - a proven, honest option.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: none from therapy; skeletal-event prevention and pain control are the craft
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort in late disease is a real road - with bone protection and pain expertise as active care, not absence of care.

Hamdy et al. ProtecT 15-year: prostate-cancer mortality 2.7% overall - 3.1% active monitoring / 2.2% prostatectomy / 2.9% RT (p=0.53); metastases 9.4/4.7/5.0%; 24.4% of the monitored arm never treated - THE FLAT LINE. NEJM 2023;388:1547-58 (PMID 36912538, verified)

Attard et al. STAMPEDE M0 abiraterone meta-analysis (n=1,974): high-risk localized/M0 - 6-yr MFS 82% vs 69% (MFS HR 0.53, OS HR 0.60); enzalutamide on top added nothing. Lancet 2022;399:447-60 (PMID 34953525, verified)

Parker et al. RADICALS-RT: adjuvant vs early-salvage post-RP RT - 5-yr bPFS 85% vs 88% (HR 1.10), adjuvant adds toxicity not control. Vale et al. ARTISTIC prospective pooled analysis: adjuvant vs early-salvage RT - EFS HR 0.95 (0.75-1.21, p=0.70); 5-yr EFS 89% vs 88% - early salvage preferred. Fizazi et al. LATITUDE final: ADT + abiraterone in mHSPC - OS 53.3 vs 36.5 months (HR 0.66). Lancet Oncol 2019;20:686-700 (PMID 30987939, verified; primary NEJM 2017 PMID 28578607)
Davis et al. ENZAMET: enzalutamide in mHSPC - OS HR 0.67, 3-yr OS 80% vs 72%. NEJM 2019;381:121-31 (PMID 31157964, verified; ARCHES rPFS HR 0.39: PMID 31329516, verified)
Chi et al. TITAN final: apalutamide in mHSPC - OS HR 0.65 (0.52 crossover-adjusted), median NR vs 52.2. JCO 2021;39:2294-303 (PMID 33914595, verified; primary PMID 31150574)
Fizazi et al. PEACE-1: ADT + docetaxel + abiraterone - overall OS HR 0.82 (p=0.030), rPFS HR 0.54; ADT+doce subpopulation OS HR 0.75. Lancet 2022;399:1695-707 (PMID 35405085, verified)
Smith et al. ARASENS: darolutamide + docetaxel + ADT - OS HR 0.68 (0.57-0.80, p<0.001). NEJM 2022;386:1132-42 (PMID 35179323, verified)

Raval et al. Systematic review of 29 real-world studies: ADT MONOTHERAPY remained the predominant mHSPC treatment across geographies despite guideline-recommended intensification - the underintensification receipt behind the ADT-alone card's deliberate last place. Smith et al. SPARTAN: apalutamide in nmCRPC - MFS 40.5 vs 16.2 (HR 0.28). NEJM 2018;378:1408-18 (PMID 29420164, verified)
Fizazi et al. ARAMIS: darolutamide in nmCRPC - MFS 40.4 vs 18.4 (HR 0.41); OS follow-up 3-yr 83% vs 77% (HR 0.69, p=0.003). NEJM 2019;380:1235-46 + NEJM 2020 (PMIDs 30763142 + 32905676, verified)
de Bono et al. PROfound: olaparib in HRR-altered mCRPC post-ARPI - Cohort A rPFS 7.4 vs 3.6 (HR 0.34). NEJM 2020;382:2091-102 (PMID 32343890, verified)

Hussain et al. PROfound OS: Cohort A 19.1 vs 14.7 months (HR 0.69, p=0.02, 66% crossover). LABEL SCOPES (secondhand, precise): olaparib+abi = BRCA ONLY (2023-05); talazoparib+enza = HRR ONLY (2023-06); olaparib mono = HRR post-ARPI. NEJM 2020;383:2345-57 (PMID 32955174, verified)

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.
INDICATE / EA8191 (NCT04423211): PET-directed salvage intensification post-RP BCR, phase 3, n=804, PFS primary, 341 US sites recruiting (ECOG-ACRIN) - registry-verified 2026-08

CCTG (NCT06592924): docetaxel addition on SUBOPTIMAL PSA response to ADT+ARPI in mCSPC, phase 3, n=830, OS primary, US sites confirmed - registry-verified 2026-08. Closures named: PSMAddition (NCT04720157) and CAPItello-281 (NCT04493853) ACTIVE NOT RECRUITING
PSMA-DC (NCT05939414): 177Lu-PSMA vs observation to delay castration in PSMA+ oligometastatic disease, phase 3, MFS primary, 144 locations (Novartis) - registry-verified 2026-08

VECTRA-01 (NCT07611110): actinium-225 PSMA-I&T (AZD2265) vs SOC in PSMA+ mCRPC post-177Lu (>=2 cycles) + taxane + ARPI, phase 3, dual rPFS/OS primaries, ECOG 0-2 - registry-verified 2026-08 (US activation early: 3 of 25 US sites open; PSMAcTION NCT06780670 is the broader post-Lu fallback)

OMAHA-003 (NCT06136624): opevesostat (MK-5684, CYP11A1) vs ARPI switch in mCRPC post-NHA + taxane, phase 3, n=1,310, OS primary, 282 locations - registry-verified 2026-08. ASCO GU 2026 presentation exists; NO peer-reviewed efficacy publication as of today - numbers deliberately not carried

EvoPAR-Prostate02 (NCT06952803): adjuvant saruparib (AZD5305) vs placebo, BRCA-mutated localized high-risk on RT+ADT, phase 3 double-blind, n=700, MFS primary, 342 locations - registry-verified 2026-08. Also named: GUIDANCE (NCT05050084) + PREDICT-RT (NCT04513717) ACTIVE NOT RECRUITING; luxdegalutamide (ARV-766) has NO phase 3 in the registry
